# ViewportScaleMode

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Graphics` · enum

```csharp
public enum ViewportScaleMode
```

How a [`ViewportScaler`](ViewportScaler.md) fits a design onto a screen of another shape.

## Values

| Value | Summary |
|---|---|
| <a name="fit"></a>`Fit` | All of the design shows, as large as fits, with bars on the sides that are left over. |
| <a name="fill"></a>`Fill` | The design fills the screen, cut off on the sides that don't fit. |
| <a name="stretch"></a>`Stretch` | The design fills the screen exactly, stretched to its shape. |
| <a name="integerfit"></a>`IntegerFit` | As [`Fit`](#fit), at a whole number of screen pixels per design pixel, for pixel art. Use it with a point sampler. |
| <a name="expand"></a>`Expand` | All of the design shows, as large as fits, and the sides that are left over show more of the world rather than bars: [`ViewportScaler.VisibleBounds`](ViewportScaler.md#visiblebounds) says how much. |
| <a name="expandvertical"></a>`ExpandVertical` | As [`Expand`](#expand) for a screen taller than the design, showing more below it, and as [`Fit`](#fit) for a wider one, with bars: for a game played upright on phones of many shapes. |
| <a name="expandhorizontal"></a>`ExpandHorizontal` | As [`Expand`](#expand) for a screen wider than the design, showing more to its right, and as [`Fit`](#fit) for a taller one, with bars: for a game played sideways on phones of many shapes. |
